newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Third crewman dies after Singapore tanker fire.
newsitem.headline: Third crewman dies after Singapore tanker fire.

text.p: A third Chinese crewman has died after an oil tanker fire in Singapore harbour on Wednesday, police said on Friday.
"One of them who was in hospital has passed away," a police spokesman said.
Earlier in the day, the body of a second crewman was recovered from the oil tanker, an official from the owners told Reuters.
"We found the body this morning and everyone's been accounted for," the official from Ocean Tanker Pte Ltd said.

The first body was found on Thursday after the blaze aboard the 26,909-dwt Singapore-registered Ocean Trader, while a fourth man is still in hospital with extensive burns. All four victims were Chinese.
The tanker was berthed at an oil terminal operated by U.S. oil company Mobil Corp when it caught fire on Wednesday evening.
Mobil said the tanker was discharging condensate, a type of light crude oil, to the Mobil refinery when the accident occurred. The cause of the blaze is not known.
"We are waiting for the green light to discharge the cargo," the Ocean Tanker official said.
